topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutation, clonal evolution and cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations arise and enable cancer development in susceptible cells within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk and how that contribution is interpreted against claims of chance or genetic susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents as causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infection can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens damage DNA and generate mutations, including the role of metabolism in determining their activity.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the conditions that promote tumour outgrowth and explain the experimental basis for that distinction.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the context of exposure determines susceptibility to carcinogens and conclude by placing that specificity within the mechanisms already discussed.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenic exposure and activity is obtained and why that evidence has limits when predicting cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and relating them to everyday decisions about cancer risk.
